exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. Practical Python 3.10-3.14 fluency track; official Python documentation and selected AnyIO/HTTPX docs reviewed 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; progressively harder typed code recall provides the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Python Fluency is practical coding retrieval, not beginner trivia or a certification. Questions use progressive recall depth: guided -> recall -> construct -> fluency. Short literals stay on one line where readable, unfamiliar data shapes and intent are explained, and most questions have one meaningful blank.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.11 added enum.StrEnum, whose members are also strings and whose str() result is the underlying string value.

reveal.text: Python 3.11 added enum.StrEnum, whose members are also strings and whose str() result is the underlying string value.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: [__________(status) for status in Status] produces plain string values when Status derives from StrEnum.

reveal.text: [str(status) for status in Status] produces plain string values when Status derives from StrEnum.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ standard-library code checks type(x) == str rather than isinstance(x, str); str(member) is the compatibility escape hatch documented for those cases.

reveal.text: Some standard-library code checks type(x) == str rather than isinstance(x, str); str(member) is the compatibility escape hatch documented for those cases.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ expresses that a method returns an instance of its own class or subclass without introducing a separate TypeVar.

reveal.text: typing.Self expresses that a method returns an instance of its own class or subclass without introducing a separate TypeVar.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ set_name(self, name: str) -> Self: ... is useful for fluent methods that return self.

reveal.text: def set_name(self, name: str) -> Self: ... is useful for fluent methods that return self.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ refers to the current enclosing class, not an arbitrary unrelated type chosen by the caller.

reveal.text: Self refers to the current enclosing class, not an arbitrary unrelated type chosen by the caller.

modules.title: Use Python 3.11 async and exception features

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.11 added ExceptionGroup plus except* clauses so independent exceptions from concurrent work can be handled by type while preserving unhandled members.

reveal.text: Python 3.11 added ExceptionGroup plus except* clauses so independent exceptions from concurrent work can be handled by type while preserving unhandled members.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________* ValueError as errors: ... handles matching ValueError members inside an exception group.

reveal.text: except* ValueError as errors: ... handles matching ValueError members inside an exception group.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ and except* cannot be mixed in the same try statement, and except* semantics differ from catching one ordinary exception object.

reveal.text: except and except* cannot be mixed in the same try statement, and except* semantics differ from catching one ordinary exception object.
